title: Imperfeito vs. perfeito
pattern: imperfeito (-ava, -ia) = was doing, used to · perfeito (-ou, -eu) = did, happened
explanation: The pretérito perfeito tells what happened, as a completed event. The imperfeito sets the scene: ongoing actions, descriptions, and habits in the past (used to). Often both appear together: the imperfeito is the background and the perfeito is what interrupted it.

examples.pt: Quando eu era criança, eu morava no Rio.
examples.en: When I was a kid, I lived in Rio.

examples.pt: Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou.
examples.en: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

examples.pt: Antigamente a gente jogava futebol todo domingo.
examples.en: We used to play soccer every Sunday.

mistake.wrong: Quando eu fui criança, eu morei na Bahia.
mistake.right: Quando eu era criança, eu morava na Bahia.
mistake.en: When I was a kid, I lived in Bahia.
mistake.reason: Childhood is a background period, so it takes the imperfeito.

title: Irregular past tense verbs
pattern: ser/ir: fui, foi · fazer: fiz, fez · ter: tive, teve · estar: estive, esteve · poder: pude, pôde
explanation: The most common verbs have irregular past forms that must be memorized. Ser and ir share the same forms (fui = I was / I went), and context tells them apart. Note that the eu and ele forms of these verbs don't carry the regular -ei/-ou endings: eu fiz, ele fez.

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the movies.

examples.pt: O que você fez no fim de semana?
examples.en: What did you do on the weekend?

examples.pt: Eu tive um problema e não pude ir.
examples.en: I had a problem and couldn't go.

mistake.reason: Fazer is irregular in the past: eu fiz, ele fez.

title: Reflexive verbs
pattern: eu me levanto · você se levanta · a gente se levanta · nós nos levantamos
explanation: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that refers back to the subject: me, te, se, nos. In Brazil the pronoun normally goes before the verb, even at the start of a sentence in speech (me chamo Ana). In casual speech some reflexive pronouns are dropped (eu levanto cedo), but se is still common.

examples.pt: A gente se encontrou na praça.

mistake.reason: The reflexive pronoun matches the subject: eu takes me, not se.

title: Object pronouns in Brazilian speech
pattern: me / te + verb (te amo, me ajuda) · speech: vi ele, conheço ela · writing: vi-o, conheço-a
explanation: Me and te go before the verb in Brazil: ele me ligou, eu te amo. For 'him', 'her' and 'them', everyday speech uses ele, ela, eles after the verb (eu vi ele), which is normal in conversation but avoided in formal writing, where o/a are used (eu o vi). Te is used with você in speech even though it's technically the tu form.

examples.pt: Você me ajuda com a mala?
examples.en: Can you help me with the suitcase?

examples.pt: Eu vi ele no mercado ontem.
examples.en: I saw him at the market yesterday.

mistake.reason: In Brazilian Portuguese, me and te go before the verb.

title: Lhe vs. pra ele
pattern: to him/her: (formal) lhe · (speech) pra ele / pra ela · to you: te / lhe
explanation: For indirect objects (to someone), formal Portuguese uses lhe. In everyday Brazilian speech, people instead say pra ele, pra ela, pra você after the verb. Lhe is still heard in polite speech meaning 'to you' (posso lhe ajudar?), but rarely for 'to him/her'.

examples.pt: Eu mandei uma mensagem pra ela.
Você pode dar o livro pra ele?
examples.en: Can you give him the book?

examples.pt: O senhor quer que eu lhe mostre o quarto?
examples.en: Would you like me to show you the room, sir?

mistake.right: Eu dei um presente pra ela.
mistake.reason: The person who receives something needs pra (or lhe); ela alone can't be an indirect object.

title: Comparatives
pattern: mais/menos + adjective + (do) que · melhor, pior, maior, menor · tão … quanto
explanation: Compare with mais (more) or menos (less) plus que or do que: mais caro do que. Bom, mau, grande and pequeno have special forms: melhor (better), pior (worse), maior (bigger), menor (smaller). For equality use tão … quanto (as … as).

examples.pt: O metrô é mais rápido do que o ônibus.
examples.en: The subway is faster than the bus.

examples.pt: Esse restaurante é melhor que aquele.
examples.en: This restaurant is better than that one.

examples.pt: Ela é tão alta quanto o irmão.
examples.en: She's as tall as her brother.

mistake.reason: Bom has its own comparative, melhor; mais bom isn't used.

title: Superlatives
pattern: o/a mais + adjective (de) · -íssimo (very, extremely) · muito + adjective
explanation: 'The most' is o/a mais + adjective, and 'in' a group is de: a cidade mais bonita do Brasil. Melhor and pior become o melhor, o pior. To say 'extremely', add -íssimo to the adjective (caro → caríssimo, lindo → lindíssimo), or just use muito.

examples.pt: Ela é a aluna mais inteligente da turma.
examples.en: She's the smartest student in the class.

examples.pt: Esse é o melhor restaurante do bairro.
examples.en: This is the best restaurant in the neighborhood.

examples.pt: O Pedro é o mais alto da família.
examples.en: Pedro is the tallest in the family.

mistake.wrong: É a cidade mais bonita em o Brasil.
mistake.right: É a cidade mais bonita do Brasil.
mistake.en: It's the most beautiful city in Brazil.
mistake.reason: After a superlative, 'in' a group or place is de, not em.

title: Por vs. para
pattern: para = destination, purpose, recipient, deadline · por = through, cause, exchange, duration
explanation: Para points toward a goal: where you're going, who something is for, why you do it. Por covers the route or means (por aqui), the cause (por causa de), exchange (obrigado por) and per (duas vezes por semana). Por merges with articles: pelo, pela.

examples.pt: Eu estudo para a prova duas vezes por semana.
examples.en: I study for the test twice a week.

mistake.reason: Thanks are 'for' something in exchange, which takes por (por + a = pela).

title: Já, ainda, ainda não, não … mais
pattern: já = already/ever · ainda = still · ainda não = not yet · não … mais = not anymore
explanation: Já means 'already' and, in questions, 'ever' (você já foi ao Rio?). Ainda means 'still', and ainda não means 'not yet'. 'Not anymore' is não … mais. Brazilians answer já-questions with the verb or with já / ainda não.

examples.pt: Ainda não, estou esperando a Ana.
examples.en: Not yet, I'm waiting for Ana.

mistake.reason: 'Not yet' is ainda não, placed before the verb.

title: Acabar de + infinitive
pattern: acabar de + infinitive = to have just done
explanation: To say something just happened, use acabar (literally 'to finish') + de + infinitive. In the present it means 'have just': acabo de chegar = I've just arrived. In speech the past is also common with the same meaning: acabei de comer.

mistake.reason: 'Just' meaning 'a moment ago' is expressed with acabar de, not só.

title: Ficar: to be located, to stay, to become
pattern: ficar em = be located · ficar = stay · ficar + adjective = get/become
explanation: Ficar is one of the most used verbs in Brazil. For fixed places it means 'to be (located)': o banco fica na esquina. It also means 'to stay' (fiquei em casa) and, with an adjective, 'to get' or 'become': fiquei nervoso.

examples.pt: Ela ficou feliz com a notícia.
examples.en: She got happy with the news.

title: Ter que / precisar + infinitive
pattern: ter que + infinitive = have to · precisar + infinitive = need to
explanation: Obligation is usually ter que (or ter de) + infinitive: tenho que trabalhar = I have to work. Precisar + infinitive means 'need to', and takes no preposition before a verb, but takes de before a noun: preciso sair, preciso de ajuda. Dever + infinitive (should) is softer advice.

examples.pt: Eu tenho que acordar cedo amanhã.
examples.en: I have to wake up early tomorrow.

examples.pt: A gente precisa de um táxi.

mistake.reason: Ter needs que (or de) before an infinitive to mean 'have to'.

title: Commands
pattern: standard: fale, coma, abra · BR speech: fala, come, abre · não + fale
explanation: The textbook command for você uses the 'opposite' vowel: falar → fale, comer → coma, abrir → abra. In much of Brazil, everyday speech uses the plain ele form instead: fala!, come!, olha! Both are understood; signs and formal requests use the standard form. Polite requests often add por favor or use pode + infinitive.

mistake.wrong: Por favor, fecha a porta, senhor.
mistake.right: Por favor, feche a porta, senhor.
mistake.reason: With senhor or in polite settings, use the standard command form (feche).

title: Algum, nenhum, todo, tudo
pattern: algum = some · nenhum = no, none · todo o/a = the whole · todos os = every · tudo = everything
explanation: Algum and nenhum agree with the noun (alguma coisa, nenhuma pessoa); nenhum after the verb needs não. Todo with an article means 'whole' or, in the plural, 'every' (todo o dia = all day, todos os dias = every day). Tudo never changes and means 'everything'.

examples.pt: Ela trabalha todos os dias, mas entende tudo.
examples.en: She works every day, but she understands everything.

mistake.reason: 'Everything' on its own is tudo; todo goes with a noun.

title: Weather and 'ago' with fazer
pattern: faz calor / frio · está chovendo · faz + time = ago / for
explanation: Weather uses fazer for heat and cold (faz frio, fez muito calor) and estar for conditions right now (está nublado, está chovendo). Fazer with a length of time means 'ago' or 'for': faz dois anos = two years ago. In speech tem is also common: tem dois anos que eu moro aqui.

examples.pt: Eu moro aqui faz dois anos.
examples.en: I've lived here for two years.

mistake.reason: Hot and cold weather is expressed with fazer, not ser.

title: Estar com fome, frio, sono
pattern: estar com + fome / sede / frio / calor / sono / medo
explanation: Where English says 'I am hungry', Portuguese says 'I am with hunger': estou com fome. The same pattern works for thirst, cold, heat, sleepiness and fear. Use muito/muita to intensify, matching the noun: com muita fome, com muito frio.

mistake.reason: Hunger is a temporary state, so it's estar com, never ser.

title: Saber vs. conhecer
pattern: saber = know facts / how to · conhecer = know people, places; meet
explanation: Saber is knowing information or a skill: sei o endereço, sei nadar. Conhecer is being familiar with a person, place or thing: conheço o Rio. In the past, conhecer often means 'met': conheci a Ana na festa.

examples.pt: Você sabe onde fica o banco?
examples.en: Do you know where the bank is?
She knows how to swim really well.

mistake.reason: Knowing a person is conhecer; saber is for facts and skills.
